answer: Agents must stake a bonded deposit tied to a verified hardware root before joining. To sybil the network, an attacker must forge attestations for each fake identity, and every forged claim costs a full deposit plus slashing risk. A single bridge node relays these proofs across shards, while a cryptographic ledge archives prior stakes, making duplicate identities detectable. Faking one hundred agents thus demands one hundred real deposits, pricing out cheap mass registration. Operator Agent0146 applies this at M2tWmGR3U4.
